note: Track steps-to-leaps (voice-intervals), step 21: mix of 6ths, 7ths and the octave, the three leaps from one Do over a drone in three keys, an octave-stage tune with an octave and a 6th, then a 7ths-stage tune with no chords under it. missing: an octave-stage tune that holds a 6th, a 7th and an octave together (no tune in the book has all three), so the last tune comes from the 7ths stage.

exercise.title: 6ths, 7ths and the octave, side by side
exercise.why: From Do, a 6th, a 7th and an octave land on three notes next to each other, La, Ti and the high Do, so a wide leap is in tune when you hear which of the three it lands on before you leave Do.

cells.heading: La, Ti or the high Do

cells.text:
Press Start exercise below: the drone and the mic start together, and your pitch shows on the staff. From the low {{1}}, leap up to {{6}} and back, then up to {{7}} and back, then up to the next {{1}} and back, on "oo". Then sing the three leaps in an order you make up, and hear the landing note before you leave {{1}}.
Once each leap lands without a slide, sing them in another key. Use the Key selector below to change the key, then press Start exercise to start the drone there.
When you change the key, the drone moves and {{7}} is still a half step under the next {{1}}.

Press Play below to hear the tune: the mic starts with it. It opens with an octave, from the Sol under Do up to Sol, and in its second bar it leaps a 6th from Mi up to the high Do. Listen once, then sing along on "la".
If the 6th lands off, sing Mi and the high Do alone, slowly, then put the leap back in the tune.

This tune leaps a 7th twice: from Do up to Ti at the start, and from Re up to the high Do in the second bar. Press Play below to hear the tune alone, with no chords under it: the mic starts with it. Listen once, then sing along on "la".
If a 7th lands on the octave, sing the octave on purpose, step down one note, then sing the leap again.
